files.semantic: GitHub Sponsors points to gschaidergabriel; no runtime/architecture behavior.

cross_source_reconciliation.content_result: Drive copies match the frozen-head contents inspected through GitHub for this shard; treat as duplicate provenance nodes, not separate semantic implementations.

release_pipeline_findings.evidence: The Docker workflow contains checkout/buildx/login/build-push steps for CPU, CUDA and Vulkan but no test, Harness, health, vulnerability scan, SBOM/signature, or acceptance-gate job before push.
release_pipeline_findings.effect: A successful container build is sufficient to publish an image even when runtime or architecture acceptance would fail.
release_pipeline_findings.required_contract: Clay 0.1 release publication must consume a verified release manifest produced only after mandatory Harness/security/boot gates pass.

release_pipeline_findings.evidence: push.paths includes Dockerfile, docker/**, requirements.txt and the workflow itself, but not ordinary core/services/config/runtime source paths despite build context '.'.
release_pipeline_findings.effect: Normal source-code changes can advance repository main without rebuilding the published container, so registry image state can lag the repository while tags still imply current product identity.
release_pipeline_findings.required_contract: Artifact identity must bind source-tree/commit digest to image digest. Relevant source changes must rebuild or explicitly invalidate the release; deployment must never infer freshness from mutable tag names.

release_pipeline_findings.evidence: The workflow directly publishes mutable latest/cpu/cuda/vulkan tags and does not record/sign a release-manifest-to-image-digest mapping in the workflow.
release_pipeline_findings.effect: A tag is not a stable artifact identity and cannot support deterministic rollback/replay by itself.
release_pipeline_findings.required_contract: Publish immutable content-addressed image digests plus signed/verified release manifest; mutable aliases may point to them only as convenience views.

release_pipeline_findings.evidence: Third-party GitHub Actions are referenced by moving major tags such as actions/checkout@v4, docker/setup-buildx-action@v3, docker/login-action@v3 and docker/build-push-action@v6 rather than immutable commit SHAs.
release_pipeline_findings.effect: Workflow dependency identity is not fully frozen by the repository commit alone.
release_pipeline_findings.required_contract: Security-sensitive release workflows should pin external actions to immutable revisions and record their identities in the release provenance.

positive_controls: Workflow permissions are explicitly scoped to contents:read and packages:write per job.
CPU, CUDA and Vulkan variants are separated rather than silently sharing one ambiguous tag.
Workflow labels preserve repository source URL metadata.
Buildx cache configuration is explicit and reproducible at the workflow level.

harness: Container publication must be downstream of Harness PASS, not merely Docker build success.
Add image boot/readiness/mandatory-child-death and artifact-identity tests to the release gate.
claycode: Model ReleaseCandidate and VerifiedRelease as typed states; mutable registry tags cannot satisfy VerifiedArtifact identity.
unifieddb: Persist source commit/tree digest -> build manifest -> image digest -> activation/rollback ancestry.
claygraph: Represent immutable build/release provenance edges and distinguish convenience aliases from artifact identity.
needle: Deployment/activation effects may consume only verified immutable release identities, never a bare latest-style tag.
frank: Runtime self-reporting of version must derive from immutable release manifest/image/source identity, not human-readable tag.
clay: One-binary/container distribution needs a single verified release transaction joining source, dependencies, tests, build output and activated artifact identity.

next: Release .github claim, then continue another non-overlapping AICORE leaf/root-file shard while global Level-0 denominator remains unfrozen.
